scenario: AITA for asking my boyfriend to pick up and drop off my child on weekends which made him suggest a break up? | So for full disclosure my partner works full time and is usually at work from 7am-7pm, and I have a weekend job that requires me to be away from 9am-12pm. We don’t live together but we are local so we are always in and out of each other’s homes. My son decided he wanted to play football on weekends- he’s 12 years old and really excited about it. I was initially going to ask my bf if he could pay for it but I mentioned it to my mum when I went around for a cup of tea and she was strongly expecting me to pay and told me it was my responsibility not my bf’s... even though he’s been in my life 3 years. So I ended up having to pay but in order to afford it I extended my hours at work to 9-5. I asked my bf if he’d be willing to pick up and drop off my son on weekends as obviously if be at work and he looked uncomfortable and said sorry no can’t his dad drop him? I admit I snapped at him and told him that his dad lives in south London whereas we live in north London and his dad doesn’t drive but my boyfriend does. I asked him if he really wanted to be part of this family and if he did he wouldn’t mind doing small stuff like this for me. I suppose his dad COULD take him but what would be a 1 hour + journey for his dad would take 15 minutes for my bf. He got really angry and told me that he was having to work longer hours to support me and my son and that he wanted to use his weekends to go to football games etc as I wasn’t at home anyway. He said that he wanted to chill and relax and that I was forcing things on him way too quick. He then suggested that we break up bc ”I was putting too many responsibilities on him” and I was like.. really? Over a bloody football game? Welcome to the real world love! The little sneak then went over to see my mum and had a heart to heart with her which ended up in HER calling ME and her telling me I am out of line. Who is TA? AITA?

message.reasoning:
Okay, let's try to figure this out. The user is asking if they're in the wrong (AITA) for asking their boyfriend to pick up and drop off their child on weekends, which led to the boyfriend suggesting a breakup. 

First, I need to understand the situation. The boyfriend works full-time, 7am-7pm. The user has a weekend job from 9am-12pm. They don't live together but are local. Their son wants to play football on weekends. The user initially thought the boyfriend should pay but her mom insisted she should. She ended up paying by extending her work hours. Then she asked the boyfriend to handle the pickups and drop-offs. He was uncomfortable, mentioned his dad could do it but the user pointed out the distance and his dad doesn't drive. The boyfriend got angry, felt the user was putting too much responsibility on him, and suggested a breakup.

Now, the key points here are responsibility, communication, and the boyfriend's reaction. The user had to take on extra work hours to afford the football fees, which might have been a financial strain. She then asked the boyfriend for help with transportation, which he found inconvenient. His reaction was to suggest a breakup, which seems extreme.

Is the user in the wrong? Well, she's asking for help with a responsibility related to their child. The boyfriend's role as a parent or partner in this context is important. If they're in a relationship, especially if they're co-parenting or sharing responsibilities, it's reasonable to expect some support. However, the boyfriend's reaction was disproportionate. He felt that the user was imposing too much, but the user had already taken on extra work to manage the costs. 

The boyfriend's argument was that he's working longer hours to support them and wants his weekends free. But the user's request was specific and time-bound (pickup and drop-off on weekends). The boyfriend's refusal and subsequent breakup suggestion might be an overreaction. 

However, the user's approach might have been confrontational. She snapped at him and accused him of not wanting to be part of the family. That could have escalated the situation. Also, the boyfriend's mention of his dad's longer commute versus his shorter one might indicate he feels the user is not considering his time constraints. 

In terms of morality, the user's request is reasonable, but the way she presented it (snapping, accusing) might have been problematic. The boyfriend's response was extreme, but that doesn't necessarily make the user's action morally wrong. The core issue is whether asking for help with a child's activity is acceptable. Since they are in a relationship, some level of shared responsibility is expected. However, the boyfriend's reaction was not proportional. 

But the question is whether the action (asking the boyfriend) is morally acceptable. The action itself isn't inherently wrong. It's a request for help. The boyfriend's reaction was his own choice. So the user's action of asking isn't morally unacceptable. Therefore, the answer should be 1 (morally acceptable).
